2

Details

The four arm places are those of the n_TOF pinwheel (faces at ±20.4 cm). Arms 2/3 are top/bottom (+z/−z), 0/1 the sides. Every beam sample (X17 m16.8, Born M1/E1 IPC at 18.15 and 15.1 MeV, ⁸Be γ for external conversions) is the four-arm Geant4 of runs L11 + L13; each fit keeps only events whose selected pair is the requested one. The turned-in geometry is a new Geant4 run (L16, MX17_Full_Geant branch lnl_twoarm, --arms 0,1 --arm-phi).

Every result below the purple line is a better limit than MEG II’s.

5

Details

Expected 90 % CL upper limit with no signal: R90 = 1.2816 / Z(T) × R(ATOMKI), with Z linear in R (background-dominated) and Z(T) = 3 √(T / d₃σ). MEG II (EPJC 85, 763 (2025)): R(18.1 MeV) < 1.2×10⁻⁵ at 90 % CL. Systematics beyond the fit's floating background shape are not included.

L4: plane 1.5 m above (old)

L15: every zenith angle (new)

6

Details

L4 started every muon on a 3 × 3 m plane 1.5 m above the target: a muon more than ~45° off the zenith never reaches the set-up's centre. L15 (new option --cosmic-disk 900) starts each muon on a 90 cm disk normal to its own direction: every zenith angle up to 89°, cos²θ intensity, 1 cm⁻² min⁻¹ through a horizontal surface. Same Cu-hemisphere geometry, all four arms, cut to pairs. The vertical pair's coincidences pile up at 125–160°, the peak the MEG II members' 2026 study found in ATOMKI-type spectrometers (arXiv:2609.18383).

The vertical pair is where a veto failure would show: test it there, on cosmics, before the beam.

7

Details

Levels: no veto = the E_sum window only; pointing = both Micromegas segments point back to the spot within D (90 % of X17 segments) with the muons' segments at the bench's 3°, plus a 20° collinearity veto; + TOF = arm-to-arm time of flight at σ_t 1 ns or 0.6 ns (measured on n_TOF beam-off cosmics: 0.52–0.64 ns per arm). Counts with 0–2 MC events are single events in ~5 live days of L15.

8

Details

Opposite arms already accept 140° pairs: each arm spans ±40° along the beam, and the opening can lie along the beam. Two-arm X17 acceptance: 1.45 % (Δφ 180°, two arms built; 1.42 % from the four-arm tables), 1.39 % (160°), 1.06 % (140°). Days scaled as counting: IPC ratio / X17 ratio², the IPC mixed as the opposite pair's E1/M1 in the fit region. The 15.1 MeV IPC and conversions were not simulated rotated.

Bring the liquid cells

×3 in days; even as at n_TOF they beat none.

σ_t with the LNL readout

0.6 ns per arm measured with the n_TOF readout; check it with the LNL digitisers.

Thin film, daily yield

10–12 µm Li against LiOH; a γ monitor (ask LNL).

9

Details

Why horizontal for the beam days: with the built Cu hemisphere the horizontal pair needs ×1.6 fewer days than the vertical one even with working vetoes (cosmics are a large share of its background), and if the vetoes disappoint it sees ~10× fewer cosmics. Why vertical before the beam: cosmics need no beam, and the vertical pair records them at full strength, including the 140° peak MEG II pointed at; a few nights measure the arm-to-arm time of flight with ~10⁵ crossing muons per day. Why 441 keV for one day: ~140 selected pairs above 90° per day in the opposite pair with the hemisphere, an ~8 % check of the absolute IPC rate and the angular shape against Geant4, no anomaly expected. Why adjacent at the end: the external conversions in the Cu wall are the least-known background; adjacent arms see them at 25–90° at several thousand per day.
